validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch (Cloudflare) so the row's own cited source could not be checked directly, and the pre-harvested wiki_citations.json is empty for this scope per the orchestrator note — there is no existing citation trail to re-verify; this is entirely fresh research. Found ZERO independent evidence that a 'Kot Momin-Jauharabad' gas pipeline exists. (1) Downloaded and visually inspected SNGPL's own official, current Transmission Network Map ('AS ON 30-06-2026', https://www.sngpl.com.pk/web/page.jsp?pgids=461 -> Transmission Network Map article -> https://www.sngpl.com.pk/web/images/transmission/TransmissionMap072026L.jpg, a 4800x7200 engineering drawing, Drawing No. T-1). Jauharabad DOES appear on the map, fed by an 8-inch line from Chashma (continuing on to Khushab/Shahpur) -- matching the diameter GEM records for P4133 and closely matching neighboring roster row P4134 'Jauharabad-Chashma Gas Pipeline' (82.21 km, 8in). 'Kot Momin' does NOT appear anywhere on this map -- not as a node, not as a line label -- including in the Bhera/Bhalwal Industrial Estate/Jhelum Crossing (Malakwal)/Sargodha corridor where Kot Momin geographically sits. (2) Checked geography: Wikipedia gives Kot Momin's coordinates as 32.18833N 73.02861E (Sargodha District, near Bhalwal, ~40km from Sargodha city, on the M2 motorway corridor) and Jauharabad's as 32.29194N 72.27361E (Khushab district HQ). These two towns are on OPPOSITE sides of Sargodha (Kot Momin to the east/southeast, Jauharabad to the west) -- there is no plausible direct transmission corridor between them on the current network, and none is drawn on SNGPL's own map. (3) The great-circle distance between the two named towns computes to ~72.0 km -- essentially identical to the GEM LengthKnown value of 72.41 km. That match (route length = straight-line town-to-town distance, not a measured pipeline route) is a classic bulk-load/geocoding artifact, exactly the failure mode flagged in this scope's orchestrator notes (implausible round/derived numbers from a single 2023-07-10 bulk load). By contrast, P4134's stated 82.21 km is close to (but sensibly longer than, i.e. plausible as an actual route atop) the ~79 km straight-line Chashma-Jauharabad distance -- P4134 looks real; P4133 does not. (4) Two independent web searches (via Bing, since WebSearch's session quota was exhausted) for 'Kot Momin' + 'Jauharabad' + gas pipeline, and 'Kot Momin' + gas pipeline + SNGPL, returned zero relevant results of any kind -- no news, no SNGPL/OGRA documentation, nothing. Conclusion: this row is very likely a fabricated/mis-parsed entity from the 2023-07 bulk load -- possibly a mangled duplicate split of the real Chashma-Jauharabad line (P4134) with a wrong start-point town substituted in, or a wholesale hallucination. PipelineType='transmission' and Owner='SNGPL' would both be plausible IF the line were real (SNGPL operates the whole Punjab network shown on this map, and 8in lines elsewhere in this bulk load are consistently classed transmission), so I am not raising separate classification/attribution flags -- the existence question is the threshold issue.
